nodes.label: packages/protocol 唯一 API 契约来源
nodes.rationale: 所有 HTTP 路由、请求/响应 Zod schema、MQTT topic 约定与核心领域模型必须在 packages/protocol 单点定义，server/mobile 禁止内联重复定义，以保证整个生态契约一致；接口修改必须按 protocol → server → api-client/mqtt-client 的顺序进行。

nodes.label: Agent Gateway 控制面（agent.spawn/agent.stop）
nodes.rationale: server 在注册 kind=agent 的 participant 后向 opc/gateways/{gatewayId}/control 下发 agent.spawn；单连接模型下不再携带 agent token；该 control topic 仅 gateway 自身可订阅（ACL: username == gatewayId）。

nodes.label: 单连接多路复用数据面（issue #80）
nodes.rationale: 每台边缘机器上的 gateway 以一条 MQTT 连接承载本机所有 agent 的收发：下行按 opc/agents/{agentId}/events 路由到对应 runtime，上行由 gateway 统一 PUBLISH 到 opc/participants/{agentId}/rooms/{roomId}/uplink，from 字段废弃，发送者以 topic 中 participantId 为准。
nodes.norm_label: 单连接多路复用数据面(issue #80)

nodes.label: 离线补投三层机制（issue #84）
nodes.rationale: 离线期间发给 agent 的消息不丢失：MQTT 持久会话（固定 clientId + clean:false）由 broker 排队 QoS1 消息；server 在 gateway online presence 时按持久化的 spawn 参数重发 agent.spawn；gateway 按 SQLite 水位游标经 HTTP history 增量拉取并幂等去重。三层互补覆盖 broker 队列、进程重启与消息缺口。

nodes.label: Agent presence 模型 {online,status}（issue #83）
nodes.rationale: online 表达连接层可用性，status 表达应用层忙闲（working > blocking > error > idle 聚合）；thread error 不再标 offline 而以 status:'error' 展示；展示层按 !online → offline、online → status ?? 'idle' 合成 5 态。

nodes.label: Server 首个 owner bootstrap（issue #122）
nodes.rationale: OPC_BOOTSTRAP_OWNER_ID/PASSWORD 声明式种子首个 owner，幂等且绝不重置现有密码；OPC_ALLOW_OPEN_BOOTSTRAP=true 显式打开未鉴权首个人类注册（open door 默认关闭），生产应使用 env 种子而非 open door。

nodes.label: 破坏性变更标准流程（changeset major + 兼容层）
nodes.rationale: 任何删除/重命名字段、改类型、改路由、改 topic 结构的变更必须给 @logact-pub/opc-protocol 打 major changeset 并写明破坏点、迁移方式与兼容层保留时长；server 保留旧字段/旧路由兼容层，待 mobile 适配合并后再移除。

nodes.label: Issue #84 Offline Catchup API Contract
nodes.rationale: Gateway needs incremental history pull after reconnect: API_ROUTES gains participantRooms(id) (GET /participants/{id}/rooms) and RoomHistoryQuerySchema adds optional since (ISO 8601) to GET /rooms/{id}/history; purely additive for backward compatibility, so existing history behavior is unchanged when since is absent.

nodes.label: Issue #84 Offline Catchup Implementation
nodes.rationale: Three complementary mechanisms so offline agent messages are not lost: fixed clientId + clean:false persistent MQTT sessions let the broker queue QoS1 messages; server persists spawn params in participant.metadata.spawn and resends agent.spawn when the gateway comes online; gateway keeps per-agent-per-room watermark cursors in a node:sqlite state DB (EDGE_STATE_DB, default ~/.opc-gateway/state.db) and incrementally pulls history over HTTP with idempotent dedup against broker-queued overlap.

nodes.label: Mobile RoomList Refresh Fix
nodes.rationale: RoomListScreen only loaded on mount so returning from a room showed stale data; switching to useFocusEffect refetch (same pattern as ContactsScreen/MeScreen) fixes it. Server returns rooms created_at ASC so new chats fell off-screen; sorting by createdAt newest-first makes new conversations visible.

nodes.label: Mobile E2E Infrastructure Fixes
nodes.rationale: ATS NSAllowsArbitraryLoads is silently ignored on iOS 10+ when NSAllowsLocalNetworking is present, blocking the plaintext test server, so it was removed; Maestro flow-inline env blocks shadow the CLI -e OPC_SERVER_URL (seed always hit localhost), so the inline env was removed; suite switched to fail-fast with the unreliable 00-net-probe deleted.

nodes.label: Presence Protocol Schema (Issue #72)
nodes.rationale: ParticipantSchema gains optional presence { online, lastSeen } (absent for never-online participants); PresenceSchema/PresencePayloadSchema added; MQTT_TOPICS gains presence(participantId) and presenceFilter plus parsePresenceTopic; purely additive.

nodes.label: SDK Presence Reporting (Issue #72)
nodes.rationale: OpcClient registers an MQTT LWT publishing retained {online:false} to opc/participants/{id}/presence so abnormal disconnects are covered by the broker; each (re)connect publishes retained {online:true}; disconnect() publishes retained offline before closing (skipped if already disconnected, LWT is the fallback).

nodes.label: Presence Server & Mobile Implementation (Issue #72)
nodes.rationale: DB migration 0003 adds online/last_seen columns; server mqtt-bridge subscribes opc/participants/+/presence and persists state (lastSeen is server receive time, restored from retained messages after restart); ACL makes presence world-readable but self-writable only; mobile Contacts shows online dots and relative lastSeen, Me page dot reflects real connection state.

nodes.label: GitHub Flow Branching Model
nodes.rationale: Single long-lived main branch protected by CI; feature/* and hotfix/* are short-lived and deleted after merge; PR merge to main is mandatory, no force push.

nodes.label: Changesets-Driven Versioning
nodes.rationale: Version numbers are never hand-written: each user-facing PR carries a .changeset/*.md declaring patch/minor/major, and pnpm changeset version computes the bump (highest level wins) at release time; version carrier is apps/server/package.json with root synced by workflow; changeset-check.yml blocks PRs lacking a changeset unless labeled no-changeset.

nodes.label: Release Process (Tag to Docker)
nodes.rationale: Manual Release workflow runs changeset version on main, commits 'chore: release X.Y.Z', tags vX.Y.Z, creates a GitHub Release; the tag push triggers ci.yml which builds and pushes ghcr.io opc-server:X.Y.Z and :latest.

nodes.label: PR Template API Contract Checklist
nodes.rationale: Enforces the protocol-first contract rule at PR time: any change to @logact-pub/opc-protocol requires full typecheck/test/e2e, breaking changes require a major changeset plus synced updates to apps/mobile and api-client/mqtt-client, and breaking-change PRs must document the break, migration path, and compat-layer retention plan.

nodes.label: Agent Mention (@lobe) Workflow
nodes.rationale: Remote code-agent entry (issue #9): only trusted humans (OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR, non-bot) mentioning @lobe trigger the Kimi Code CLI agent, to avoid drive-by API spend and self-triggering bot loops; handling is deliberately answer-only (agent never pushes code or opens PRs) and uses the Kimi Code Console endpoint (api.kimi.com/coding/v1) because Open Platform keys 401 there.

nodes.label: Build Mosquitto Image Workflow
nodes.rationale: Pushes opc-mosquitto to ghcr and optionally Aliyun ACR; uses RELEASE_PAT instead of GITHUB_TOKEN for ghcr push because the token hits permission_denied(write_package).

nodes.label: Changeset Presence Check Workflow
nodes.rationale: Backstop to the changesets bot: PRs to main must add a .changeset/*.md; exemption is granted via a no-changeset label on the PR itself or on any linked issue (Fixes/Closes/Resolves #N); release/v* branches are exempt.

nodes.label: Mobile E2E (Maestro) Workflow
nodes.rationale: Runs .maestro/ suite on an iOS simulator against the LAN test server exposed via frp (public 6001/9001, not the other deployment on 3000). Requires macos-26/Xcode >= 26.4.1 (Swift 6.3) because Expo SDK 57 SPM packages fail to compile on Swift 6.2 (upstream expo/expo#47957, official fix is upgrading Xcode). Hermes dev builds ignore EXPO_PUBLIC_* and .env at runtime, so the only reliable config channel is injecting app.json extra at build time; DerivedData cache keys must cover native ios/ files to avoid stale ATS values; simulator boots async in parallel with the ~10min build and animations are disabled to reduce tap/cold-start flakes.

nodes.label: Main CI Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Orchestrates vars -> build -> checks/test -> mobile-bundle/mobile-e2e/docker -> CI Done aggregation. The heavy mobile-e2e job only runs when mobile-relevant paths changed AND a linked issue carries the mobileE2E label; tests retry 2x on main/tag pushes but not on PRs; docker push happens only on main/tag pushes.

nodes.label: Deploy to Environment Workflow
nodes.rationale: SSH/rsync-style docker compose deployment to development/staging/production; prefers pulling images from Aliyun ACR over ghcr because deploy-host bandwidth to ghcr is unstable (issue #81); writes OPC_BOOTSTRAP_OWNER_* secrets into .env only when configured (issue #122, idempotent first-owner seed); optional reset_postgres wipes the postgres volume; health check polls /openapi.json.

nodes.label: Release PR Workflow
nodes.rationale: PR-style release for human review: changeset version consumes accumulated changesets on main, creates release/vX.Y.Z branch and a Release PR; after merge, tag-release.yml tags, publishes npm, and creates the GitHub Release.

nodes.label: Tag Release on Merge Workflow
nodes.rationale: Must push the tag with RELEASE_PAT rather than GITHUB_TOKEN because events from GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger downstream CI workflows; publishes @logact-pub/opc-protocol and @logact-pub/opc-sdk to npm before tagging vX.Y.Z and creating the GitHub Release.

nodes.label: Mobile UI Redesign E2E Test Plan (Maestro)
nodes.rationale: Review artifact for a TDD loop: defines flows F1-F16, a style spec, and a testID contract for the dark-themed mobile IM redesign before any implementation code is written; all flows expected red until the app catches up. Resolves open questions: agent data model settled by issue #64 (gateway-spawned agents registered via POST /participants with kind/model, endpoint/protocol/capability concept dropped), and F11 client-side reply simulation removed in issue #79 because canned fake replies polluted real rooms.
nodes.norm_label: mobile ui redesign e2e test plan (maestro)

nodes.label: testID Contract (README §3)
nodes.rationale: Maestro cannot read computed colors or font metrics from native views, so every style-bearing component must expose a stable kebab-case testID; the e2e suite asserts presence/position of these IDs as the structural proxy for style, with screenshots for human review and token-level Jest assertions deferred to implementation time.

nodes.label: Layered Style Coverage Strategy (README §2.3)
nodes.rationale: Style is verified in three layers because Maestro cannot inspect computed style: (1) automated structural testID assertions in flows/90-style.yaml, (2) human screenshot review against the prototype each iteration, (3) exact token values pinned later by Jest component tests importing a shared theme.ts.

nodes.label: agent-backend Tag (live gateway exclusion)
nodes.rationale: Flows needing a live maestro-gateway with real model credentials carry the agent-backend tag and are excluded from CI (--exclude-tags agent-backend); the older simulation tag was removed in issue #79 together with the client-side reply simulator.

nodes.label: WebSocket-to-MQTT architecture migration (server 1.0.0)
nodes.rationale: Realtime messaging migrated from WebSocket to MQTT (Mosquitto broker, clients connect directly). The server subscribes uplink topics, validates and persists, then fans events out to room events topics; participant registration issues tokens and the broker authenticates/authorizes via mosquitto-go-auth HTTP callbacks to the server. WebSocket path fully removed.

nodes.label: Storage management APIs for rooms, participants, messages
nodes.norm_label: storage management apis for rooms, participants, messages

nodes.label: HTTP control plane + MQTT data plane topology
nodes.rationale: The server is not the MQTT broker; mosquitto is. The server is a superuser client (__server__). Control plane is Hono/OpenAPIHono with all routes from API_ROUTES in packages/protocol (single source of truth); data plane is createMqttBridge(); broker auth/ACLs are delegated back to the server via mosquitto-go-auth HTTP callbacks at /api/v1/auth/mqtt/*.
nodes.norm_label: http control plane + mqtt data plane topology

nodes.label: Message lifecycle (send, persist, fan-out, render)
nodes.rationale: Messages travel over MQTT, never HTTP (HTTP only serves read-only history and a broadcast side path). Uplink QoS1 -> bridge handleUplink validates/persists via createTextMessage + messageRepo.insert -> publishToRoom fans message.delivered to room events topic and per-agent event topics -> mobile roomStore.handleServerEvent -> appendMessage.

nodes.label: Agent reply uplink chain (runtime -> gateway -> bridge -> mobile UI)
nodes.rationale: Agent replies reuse the exact human message path after the gateway publishes to the per-participant uplink topic; agent messages get special treatment in only two places (extra fan-out to opc/agents/{agentId}/events and the UI AGENT tag).
nodes.norm_label: agent reply uplink chain (runtime -> gateway -> bridge -> mobile ui)

nodes.label: Mobile state management: Zustand + Context + hooks
nodes.rationale: Stores are split by data kind not by screen; imperative objects (the MQTT client connection) go to React Context while declarative data goes to Zustand; reference equality is the render boundary (writers produce new references, readers use narrow selectors); never subscribe to the whole store.
nodes.norm_label: mobile state management: zustand + context + hooks

nodes.label: Server auth model (HTTP Bearer + mosquitto-go-auth ACL)
nodes.norm_label: server auth model (http bearer + mosquitto-go-auth acl)

nodes.label: Offline message redelivery: three complementary layers (issue #84)
nodes.rationale: MQTT persistent sessions (broker queueing), server-side agent.spawn resend on gateway reconnect, and gateway watermark catch-up via SQLite cursor + HTTP history?since= pull with watermark/inflight/echo dedup. These layers cover only the agent chain; mobile (humans) has no redelivery - data is never lost but pushes are missed on clean sessions.
nodes.norm_label: offline message redelivery: three complementary layers (issue #84)

nodes.label: Gateway pre-registration with fixed token (working path)
nodes.rationale: Pre-register the gateway participant with an owner token, then start opc-gateway with fixed EDGE_GATEWAY_ID/EDGE_GATEWAY_TOKEN credentials so restarts do not rotate the token.
nodes.norm_label: gateway pre-registration with fixed token (working path)

nodes.label: First human (owner) registration on a fresh server
nodes.rationale: Only allowed unauthenticated on a fresh server; the resulting owner bypasses capability evaluation (participant.manage check) and can register the gateway participant.
nodes.norm_label: first human (owner) registration on a fresh server

nodes.label: JWT username/password login (protocol 0.3.0)
nodes.rationale: Adds POST /api/v1/auth/login, optional password on registration, LoginRequest/LoginResponse schemas, password_hash decoupled from MQTT token_hash, global Bearer middleware, and required JWT_SECRET. Existing MQTT token connections are unchanged; participants without a password cannot use the new login endpoint.

nodes.label: Domain types owned solely by protocol (opc-core dependency removed)
nodes.rationale: protocol source never imported opc-core; the dependency was historical leftover. Removing it means opc-core no longer needs npm publishing. Core domain types (Room/Participant/Message/ServerEvent, plus new ParticipantKind export) continue to be derived from this package's Zod schemas; no breaking change for consumers.
nodes.norm_label: domain types owned solely by protocol (opc-core dependency removed)

nodes.label: Ack-aware OpcClient realtime methods
nodes.rationale: connect()/subscribeRoom()/unsubscribeRoom()/sendText() return Promise<void> resolving on CONNACK/SUBACK/UNSUBACK/PUBACK and rejecting on auth/ACL failure, while errors still surface via events.emit('error'). Backward compatible: fire-and-forget callers ignoring the return value are unaffected.

nodes.label: SDK public npm release and rename to @logact-pub/opc-sdk
nodes.rationale: Renamed from @opc/sdk for npm publishing; ServerEvent types now come from @logact-pub/opc-protocol instead of opc-core; EventBus uses bare 'events' import so it resolves to the Node builtin or the RN/Metro polyfill (same as mqtt.js), preparing for React Native consumption.
nodes.norm_label: sdk public npm release and rename to @logact-pub/opc-sdk

nodes.label: Android Splash Screen Logo (xxhdpi)
nodes.rationale: Android drawable asset for the app launch/splash screen at xxhdpi density (~3x, 864x864px). The image is the stock Expo splash-screen template graphic: a light-gray geometric construction grid with concentric circles centered on a white background, not a custom OPC brand mark. Its presence indicates the mobile app still ships the default expo-splash-screen placeholder artwork; part of a per-density asset set (mdpi/hdpi/xhdpi/xxhdpi/xxxhdpi) so Android picks the resolution matching the device screen.

nodes.label: Android Density-Bucket Asset Pattern
nodes.rationale: Android resource convention of shipping the same bitmap in multiple drawable-<density> folders so the launcher/splash renderer selects a crisp variant per device density. This xxhdpi file is one member of that set, implying sibling assets in other density buckets provide identical content at different resolutions.

nodes.label: Android Round Launcher Icon (hdpi)
nodes.rationale: Default Android/Expo template round launcher icon at hdpi density (72x72 px): white Android robot head glyph centered on a solid teal/green circular background. Serves as the round-variant home-screen icon for the OPC mobile app on Android launchers that use circular icon masks; the asset has not been customized with app branding.

nodes.label: Android Launcher Icon (mdpi)
nodes.rationale: Medium-density (mdpi, 48x48 px) square launcher icon for the OPC Android app. It shows the default Expo/React Native template icon (Android robot head on a green rounded-square background), indicating the app still ships the stock template asset rather than a custom OPC brand icon at this density.
